answer: Agents secure 1,000 distinct units of verified work by solving iterative puzzles across a frozen ridge. An honest agent pays 1x cost, while 1,000 fakes must forge 1,000x the unique computational load. A verifier checks every output against a tundra baseline to ensure non-replayable utility. If an agent fails the logic audit, a permanent burn occurs. This mechanism prevents pooling by requiring fresh work per identity.
